tools.name: redbeam_open_file
tools.description: Open a PDF drawing set in REDBEAM as a tab of YOUR OWN, behind whatever the person is looking at: nothing on their screen moves, REDBEAM does not come to the front, and the keyboard stays where it is. Your tabs sit in a group under your name and colour. Later calls that name no `file` go to the PDF you opened last. If the person already has this PDF open, it is not opened twice: the answer says `yours:false`, which only means the tab stays theirs. You work in it exactly as in your own, through your own view: every read, screenshot, page turn and write works, and nothing asks them. Its takeoff is read from the PDF itself. Returns {accepted:true} — NOT "opened": rendering a large set takes a few seconds, so poll redbeam_get_ui_state until pageCount is above zero before drawing or reading quantities, or pass wait:true to be answered once it has opened.

path.description: Absolute path to a .pdf on this computer.

wait.description: Answer once the PDF has opened ({opened:true, pageCount, yours}) instead of at once. Waits up to about 20 seconds; a very large set may still answer opened:false, then poll redbeam_get_ui_state.

tools.name: redbeam_screenshot
tools.description: PNG of a sheet. With no `page`: YOUR sheet (the one your session is on; redbeam_go_to_page turns it, and the person's screen is not touched), showing the box you last framed with redbeam_zoom_to_region, or the whole sheet, with markups drawn. Name the PDF with `file` and the sheet with `page` and that sheet is rendered on its own, sharp, without turning anything, so several can be asked for at once and none waits on another. With `region`: a close-up of that box of the sheet rendered fresh by PDFium at `width` pixels, sharp at any zoom — use it to read a tag, a note or a dimension rather than cropping a whole-sheet screenshot. Find the box with find_text or get_words. Needs a window with a document open. With `path` (ending .png) the picture is written to that file instead of sent back, and the answer is only {saved, path}: a check image with the layout on it, kept without filling your context.

width.description: Output width in pixels (height follows the box). Default 1200 for a region, 1600 for a whole sheet; 600-800 is plenty to read a tag, 2000+ for fine print. At most 6000.

page.description: The sheet: a ZERO-based page number, or its sheet code as the set prints it ("A4.0"). Rendered on its own without turning the window. Defaults to the sheet showing.

tools.name: redbeam_set_title_blocks
tools.description: Name every sheet of the open set from two boxes on its title block, the way a person does with Read from title block: `numberBox` around the drawing (sheet) number and `titleBox` around the drawing title, normalized like get_words. Every sheet is read in those two places, in the background; the names replace the bookmark, page label and automatic reading in list_sheets, and on save they are written into the PDF as its page labels, so Bluebeam shows them too. The answer shows what the boxes read on `page` (default: the sheet showing) and on a sample of other sheets, so a box that caught the wrong field is seen before trusting it. Find the boxes first with get_words on one sheet's title block. `clear: true` removes the boxes. Not on the undo stack: call again to change. Needs a window.

numberBox.description: The box around the drawing number on the title block: {x0,y0,x1,y1} in NORMALIZED [0,1] page coordinates, y DOWN from the top, NOT PDF points (the space get_words and find_text report boxes in). Only words whose centre is inside are read.

titleBox.description: The box around the drawing title (optional; leave out to read numbers only) on the title block: {x0,y0,x1,y1} in NORMALIZED [0,1] page coordinates, y DOWN from the top, NOT PDF points (the space get_words and find_text report boxes in). Only words whose centre is inside are read.

page.description: ZERO-based. The sheet to preview the boxes on; default the one showing.

clear.description: Remove the title block boxes; names set with rename_sheets stay.

Read from the PDF's vector paths. Use it to measure a wall, a ceiling grid or a panel off the drawing itself. Lines are cut to the box: a line that goes on past it comes back as the part inside, marked `cut: true` (whole:true returns it as drawn). Filter to lines fully inside the box, an angle, horizontal or vertical, or a length range; a segment drawn twice is returned once. Keep the box small. Needs a window. page.description: ZERO-based page to show first.

inside.description: For get_lines: only lines with both ends inside rect. Default false (lines crossing it are included, cut to rect).

angleTolerance.description: For get_lines orientation or angle, in degrees. Default 1.

dedupe.description: For get_lines: merge a segment drawn twice, in either direction. Default true.

sort.description: For get_lines: longest first (default), left to right, or top to bottom.

maxLengthPoints.description: For get_lines: leave out longer segments, in PDF points.

minLengthFeet.description: For get_lines on a scaled sheet: shortest length kept, in feet.

maxLengthFeet.description: For get_lines on a scaled sheet: longest length kept, in feet.

whole.description: Return each line whole, as drawn, even where it goes on past rect. Default false: cut to rect.

angle.description: Only lines at this angle, degrees 0..180 with y down (as the answer reports angles), within angleTolerance.

tools.name: redbeam_get_bom
tools.description: The bill of materials — what to ORDER, per scope: the deliverable a takeoff exists to produce, computed from the same roll-up the panel renders. Read `confidence` per line before quoting any number: a `blocked` line carries quantity null (the scope is missing something, and 0 would be a claim), and an `unverified` line is a count this build has never checked against the Qt original. `totals` deliberately sums VERIFIED lines only, so it does not agree with adding the rows up — a total that mixes a checked number with an unchecked one hides which is which. Needs a window. Empty until pages are calibrated. Ask for less: `scope` (a name), `scopeId` or `scopeIds` returns only those scopes' lines; `brief` says each scope's note once (in `notes`) instead of on every line. `perArea` adds `areas`: every area of those scopes laid out on its own, with its sheet and its counts keyed as `areaItems` names them, to compare drawn and counted numbers room by room. `longerThanStock` names each scope whose runs are longer than the stock they are cut from (jointed in the field), with the shortest stock in whole feet that would run them without joints. `perimeter` adds `perimeters`: per scope and sheet, the frame round the whole field (every area's edges less the stretches two areas share, such as the fold line between chevron wings) and those shared edges on their own, in feet.

scope.description: Only the scopes with this name (whole name first, else any name containing it).

scopeId.description: Only this scope.

perArea.description: Also count every area on its own (`areas`).

brief.description: Each scope's note once, in `notes`, not on every line.

perimeter.description: Also give the frame round each scope's field per sheet, shared edges counted once and apart.

file.description: Optional on every call: the PDF this call is about, as a full path, file name or document id. REDBEAM keeps several PDFs open at once and the call goes to this one, whichever the person is looking at. Leave it out and the call goes to the PDF you opened or named last, so name it whenever you work in more than one. Every result names the file it acted on.

tools.name: redbeam_export
tools.description: Produce the takeoff package. `tsv` is the pricing sheet and `report` is the branded self-contained HTML; both come back as TEXT in the reply rather than as a saved file, because the buttons hand a blob to the browser's downloader and put it somewhere an agent can neither read nor choose — write the string yourself if you want a file. `marked-pdf` is the exception: it writes the OPEN drawing with its markups on it to the `path` you give, reports only whether it was written, and covers one document, not the project. Needs a window. The ESTIMATE exports — `csv`, `estimate-tsv` and `pdf` — cover one round: every scope with its measured quantity and its components. csv and estimate-tsv return content; pdf renders the branded document with a picture of every sheet that carries takeoff and writes it to the `path` you give. marked-pdf and pdf NEED `path`: REDBEAM never puts a Save dialog in front of the person on an agent's behalf. With `path`, any format is written to that file instead (its folder must exist; nothing is replaced unless overwrite, never a PDF). pieces-csv is the piece list of every run product.

what.description: tsv, report, csv and estimate-tsv return content; marked-pdf and pdf write a file to `path` (required for them) and return {saved:true}.

estimateId.description: For csv, estimate-tsv and pdf: which round. Defaults to the open one.

path.description: For export: an absolute path to write the file to, e.g. C:\\Users\\me\\Desktop\\takeoff.csv. Its folder must exist. Without it, text formats come back in the reply.

overwrite.description: For export with path: replace a file already there. A PDF is never replaced.

productType.description: For create_scope, update_scope and describe_product: panels, planks, baffle_cassette, baffle, linear_parts, custom_assembly, or custom_pattern (beta: a product an agent designs as a recipe; see describe_product {productType:"custom_pattern"}). Decides what the scope is measured as, so create_scope needs no scopeType with it. describe_product without it lists every product.

tools.name: redbeam_set_pattern_origin
tools.description: Set where an area's pattern starts: at a point, a corner, the nearest point on an edge or line, the centre, the nearest crossing of the grid drawn in the area (mode grid), or back to automatic. Applies to the area at `point`, to markupId(s), or to every area of the scope on the sheet showing. Read it back with redbeam_get_pattern. Needs a window.

scopeId.description: For set_active_scope, create_markup, reassign_markup, set_scope_direction, update_scope, duplicate_scope, archive_scope and commit_scope. Defaults to the active scope where one makes sense.

markupId.description: For set_pattern_origin and set_pattern_direction (applyTo area): the area. Without it, `point` picks the area, else every area of the scope on the sheet showing.

mode.description: For set_pattern_origin: point (start exactly at `point`, inside the area), corner (the area's corner named by `corner`, or the one nearest `point`), edge (the point on the area's edge nearest `point`, so the first member sits on that edge or line), center (the middle of the area), grid (the crossing of the grid DRAWN in the area nearest `point`, else nearest the corner the layout starts from or `corner`; the answer gives the grid's angle and module and how far the start moved), auto (clear it; the layout chooses the best start).

point.description: {x,y}, normalized. For set_pattern_origin (where, and which area: the area containing it), set_pattern_direction with applyTo area, and trace_area (a point inside the field to trace).

file.description: Optional on every call: the PDF this call is about, as a full path, file name or document id. REDBEAM keeps several PDFs open at once and the call goes to this one, whichever the person is looking at. Leave it out and the call goes to the PDF you opened or named last, so name it whenever you work in more than one. Every result names the file it acted on.

angle.description: For set_pattern_origin mode grid and detect_grid: read only grid lines at this angle (degrees, y down) and at right angles to it. Default: the strongest angle drawn.

tools.name: redbeam_set_pattern_direction
tools.description: Set the direction the members run, for the whole scope, the sheet showing, or one area, as two points along a member (x1,y1,x2,y2, normalized) or an angle. Area beats sheet beats scope. Laid-out products count nothing until a direction is set. Needs a window.

scopeId.description: For set_active_scope, create_markup, reassign_markup, set_scope_direction, update_scope, duplicate_scope, archive_scope and commit_scope. Defaults to the active scope where one makes sense.

applyTo.description: For set_pattern_direction: the whole scope (default), every area of the scope on the sheet showing, or one area (markupId or point). Area beats page beats scope.

markupId.description: For set_pattern_origin and set_pattern_direction (applyTo area): the area. Without it, `point` picks the area, else every area of the scope on the sheet showing.

point.description: {x,y}, normalized. For set_pattern_origin (where, and which area: the area containing it), set_pattern_direction with applyTo area, and trace_area (a point inside the field to trace).

angle.description: For set_pattern_direction instead of x1..y2: the direction members run, in degrees on the sheet: 0 across, 90 up it.

file.description: Optional on every call: the PDF this call is about, as a full path, file name or document id. REDBEAM keeps several PDFs open at once and the call goes to this one, whichever the person is looking at. Leave it out and the call goes to the PDF you opened or named last, so name it whenever you work in more than one. Every result names the file it acted on.

tools.name: redbeam_trace_field
tools.description: A hatched or patterned field (a wood slat, baffle or cassette ceiling, a tiled or textured finish) traced from the pattern itself, for a field with no line drawn around it, where trace_area says it landed on drawing content and get_lines returns thousands of strokes. Give a point inside the field. REDBEAM finds the pattern's stroke direction there, joins the strokes into a solid field (bridging the breaks a dashed hatch has at every grid line, column and panel joint, and ignoring grid lines, dimensions, text and walls at other angles), and returns its outline where the strokes stop, as normalized rings ready for create_markup, with its area. Columns, light troughs and shafts the pattern stops around come back as cutouts (holes in the rings, listed under `cutouts`); specks smaller than minCutoutSqFt are filled. It then checks the outline against the sheet as rendered: strokes painted over in white are cut out and flagged, and `onTheSheet` says how dark the field is, how much of the band just past its edge looks the same (`edgeContinues`, 0 is a clean edge) and how much of it the sheet shows blank. Every outline is also checked for crossing itself and for points in the title block; `warnings` says so. all:true also returns every other field of the same pattern on the sheet (rooms of the same ceiling separated by walls). Look at each field's `lookAt` box with redbeam_screenshot (region, overlay on) before you trust an edge. Reads the whole sheet unless `rect` narrows it. create:true places each field as an area of scopeId (or your scope), one undo step. Needs a window.

page.description: ZERO-based page to show first.

rect.description: Optional {x0,y0,x1,y1}, normalized: only look inside this box. Default the whole sheet.

all.description: Also return every other field of the same pattern on the sheet (or in rect). Default false: the field at point only.

angle.description: The pattern's stroke direction in degrees, 0..180, y down, as get_lines reports angles. Default: read at point (of the strongest directions there, the finest pattern).

bridgeGapFeet.description: The widest gap between neighbouring strokes still inside the field, in feet. Default: measured at point.

minWidthFeet.description: Parts of the pattern narrower than this are not field (a wall drawn with the same hatch, a neck between two rooms). Default 1.25.

minCutoutSqFt.description: Holes smaller than this are filled (a sprinkler, a tag); larger ones are cutouts. Default 1.5.

minFieldSqFt.description: With all: the smallest other field returned. Default 1% of the field at point.

tools.name: redbeam_invoke_ui_action
tools.description: Drive the app the way a person would. Custom patterns (beta): preview_pattern, save_pattern, clear_pattern_preview, list_patterns, use_pattern. Navigation and reads: set_tool, set_active_scope, go_to_page, set_layout_preview, open_panel, get_scale_presets, get_bom, export. Reading the sheets: list_sheets (sheet number and title per page, and where each came from), set_title_blocks (name every sheet from a number box and a title box on the title block), rename_sheets (name pages yourself), find_text (where text is, with boxes), get_words (every word on a page with its box), zoom_to_region (frame and mark a box in the window), set_markup_visibility (hide the PDF's own markups and/or REDBEAM's for a clean look; nothing is written). Measuring without drawing: measure (distance or area between points at the sheet's scale), get_lines (the drawing's own line segments in a box). Working on a copy: save_copy (a copy of the open PDF beside it, the original untouched; withoutEmbeddedMarkups leaves other apps' markups out). Setting a product up: describe_product (every input a product needs: key, unit key, units, default). Patterns: set_pattern_origin, set_pattern_direction, get_pattern. Reading the drawing: trace_area (the closed outline around a point), detect_pattern (spacing, member length, runs and rows of a drawn pattern), detect_grid (module, rows, columns and first crossing of a drawn panel or tile grid), read_scale (scales the sheets state, and a check against a written dimension), track_addenda (sheets replaced by a later issue, and scopes on them). Writing many: create_markups (one call, one undo step). Output: get_piece_list (runs, cut lengths, stock use, parts), get_history (who changed what and when; kept in the PDF). Takeoff writes: create_markup, delete_markup, set_calibration, reassign_markup, set_scope_direction. Setting a takeoff up: create_scope, update_scope, duplicate_scope, archive_scope, set_page_scale, begin_scale_region, set_region_scale, cancel_scale_region, delete_scale_region. Saving an answer now (the app also saves each scope by itself once a change settles): commit_scope. Everything goes through the same handlers a click uses, so writes land on the undo stack with an origin of `agent` and are broadcast to other windows — a takeoff change is never invisible to the person who owns it. THE EXCEPTIONS, by name: set_title_blocks and rename_sheets are not undone (call them again to change a name); commit_scope is a RECORD rather than an edit and is superseded rather than undone; set_page_scale, begin_scale_region/set_region_scale and delete_scale_region are project setup that the undo stack has never covered, for the buttons either — so a scale written over a range CANNOT be taken back, and overwriting one nobody asked you to change silently re-measures every markup on those sheets. Read the existing scale first. Saving and undo: save (write the takeoff into the PDF now and say how it went), undo, redo. Settings: get_settings, set_setting. Editing: update_markup (reshape or move), duplicate_markups, select_markups, create_dimension, rotate_pages. Other PDFs: import_scopes. The PDF's own content: list_annotations, list_links, list_bookmarks, accept_imported. Tabs: close_tab. Lists: list_markups, list_scopes. Every action here also has a tool of its own named redbeam_<action>, with only its own inputs; prefer those.

scopeId.description: For set_active_scope, create_markup, reassign_markup, set_scope_direction, update_scope, duplicate_scope, archive_scope and commit_scope. Defaults to the active scope where one makes sense.

page.description: The sheet: a ZERO-based page number, or the sheet number as the set prints it ("A4.0"). On a write that acts on a sheet (create_markup, set_calibration, set_scope_direction, set_pattern_origin, set_pattern_direction, begin_scale_region) the call shows that sheet first and lands there; without it the write lands on the sheet showing. Also for go_to_page, get_words, find_text, zoom_to_region, measure, get_lines, detect_pattern, trace_area, read_scale, list_links, list_annotations, list_markups, rotate_pages and track_addenda.

panel.description: For open_panel: scope, settings, or none (closes them all). bom and browser are from the old project mode and are refused with what to use instead.

what.description: For export: tsv, report, marked-pdf, csv, estimate-tsv, pdf or pieces-csv. See redbeam_export.

estimateId.description: For export csv, estimate-tsv and pdf: which round. Defaults to the open one.

label.description: For create_scope and update_scope, the name on the shelf — must be unique, because two scopes with one label are indistinguishable everywhere it matters and rescoping into the wrong one is silent. For set_region_scale, what the region IS ("Detail 3 / head").

scopeType.description: For create_scope and update_scope. A scope counts only the markup kind it is typed for, so changing it on a scope that already has takeoff does not convert that takeoff — it stops it reaching any quantity.

color.description: For create_scope and update_scope. CSS hex.

specifications.description: For create_scope and update_scope: the product spec. On update it is MERGED, never replaced — this same object also carries the pattern directions the direction tool writes, and replacing it would silently re-orient every piece count on the scope. Set a key to null to remove it.

archived.description: For archive_scope; default true. Archiving hides a scope, it does not destroy it — its markups stay and un-archiving restores the quantities exactly.

presetId.description: For set_page_scale and set_region_scale: a named title-block scale, e.g. `arch-1-8`. Call get_scale_presets — the ids are not guessable and a stated scale needs no measuring, so this covers a whole sheet series where the reference-line tool covers one page.

feetPerPoint.description: For set_page_scale and set_region_scale, instead of presetId: drawing feet per PDF point. Prefer presetId when the title block states a scale, so the stored source records that it was stated, not measured.

pages.description: For set_page_scale and find_text: explicit ZERO-based page numbers in the OPEN document. set_page_scale defaults to the open sheet and writes them in ONE transaction: half a range carrying a new scale and half the old one is a set where some sheets measure and some do not, with nothing saying which. find_text defaults to every page.

fromPage.description: For set_page_scale and find_text: start of an inclusive ZERO-based range.

toPage.description: For set_page_scale and find_text: end of an inclusive ZERO-based range. For duplicate_markups: the sheet the copies go on (default: their own).

rect.description: For begin_scale_region, zoom_to_region and get_words: {x0,y0,x1,y1} in NORMALIZED [0,1] page coordinates, y DOWN from the top, NOT PDF points — the same space find_text reports boxes in. For begin_scale_region, a region carries its own scale for the details sheet where four details sit at four scales; drawing it is only half the gesture — it governs nothing until set_region_scale answers the picker it opens. For get_words, only the words whose centre is inside. For get_lines, the box to read linework from; keep it small. For trace_field: only look inside this box (default the whole sheet).

kind.description: For create_markup: area, cutout, polyline, count or shape. For list_markups: only this kind.

rings.description: For create_markup: [[{x,y}, …]] in NORMALIZED [0,1] page coordinates, NOT PDF points. An area takes more rings as holes. A vertex may carry `bulge` (tan of a quarter of the arc's sweep, + counter-clockwise; 1 is a half circle) for a true arc to the next vertex, and a ring may be {circle:{cx,cy,r}} with r as a fraction of the page width. Page points are rejected rather than placed off the sheet. For update_markup: the new shape.

id.description: For delete_markup, reassign_markup and delete_scale_region. Region ids are reported as `scaleRegions` by redbeam_get_ui_state and nowhere else. For get_history: only this markup or scope. For update_markup: the markup to change. To remove one hole of an area, give the hole id a cutout answered with: cut:<area id>:<hole number, from 1>.

value.description: For set_calibration: the real length, e.g. "10" or "7 1/2". For set_setting: the new value.

unit.description: For set_calibration: in, ft, mm, cm, m.

lengthPdfPoints.description: For set_calibration: measured length of the reference, in PDF points.

sheet.description: For go_to_page instead of page: the sheet number as the set prints it, e.g. "A4.0". Punctuation and case are ignored ("A.4.0" finds A4.0); a code that matches no sheet, or more than one, is refused rather than guessed.

query.description: For find_text: the text to find, e.g. a tag like "C-7".

wholeWord.description: For find_text: only whole words, so "C-7" does not also find C-70. Default false.

limit.description: For find_text (default 300 matches), get_words (default 3000 words) and get_lines (default 300 lines). get_history: default 200 events. get_piece_list: default 1000 runs. list_markups: default 500.

margin.description: For zoom_to_region: room left around the box, as a fraction of its size. Default 0.15.

highlight.description: For zoom_to_region: mark the box the way a search hit is marked. Default true.

embedded.description: For set_markup_visibility: false hides the PDF's own markups (Bluebeam's or anyone's), true shows them. Omit to leave as is.

redbeam.description: For set_markup_visibility: false hides REDBEAM's takeoff, dimensions and layout drawn over the sheet, true shows them. The takeoff itself is untouched.

points.description: For measure: two or more {x,y} in NORMALIZED [0,1] page coordinates, y down. Nothing is drawn or written. For set_calibration: the two ends of the reference, instead of lengthPdfPoints. For create_dimension: its two ends.

closed.description: For measure: close the shape back to the first point and also give its area. Default false.

minLengthPoints.description: For get_lines: leave out segments shorter than this, in PDF points. Default 2 (hatching and text strokes).

name.description: For save_copy: the copy's file name. Defaults to "<name> (takeoff).pdf"; a free name is found if it is taken. May include a folder under the open file's folder (made if missing), or be a full path to a folder that exists.

productType.description: For create_scope, update_scope and describe_product: panels, planks, baffle_cassette, baffle, linear_parts, custom_assembly, or custom_pattern (beta: a product an agent designs as a recipe; see describe_product {productType:"custom_pattern"}). mode.description: For set_pattern_origin: point (start exactly at `point`, inside the area), corner (the area's corner named by `corner`, or the one nearest `point`), edge (the point on the area's edge nearest `point`, so the first member sits on that edge or line), center (the middle of the area), auto (clear it; the layout chooses the best start).

point.description: {x,y}, normalized. For set_pattern_origin (where, and which area: the area containing it), set_pattern_direction with applyTo area, trace_area and trace_field (a point inside the field to trace).

markupId.description: For set_pattern_origin and set_pattern_direction (applyTo area): the area. Without it, `point` picks the area, else every area of the scope on the sheet showing.

applyTo.description: For set_pattern_direction: the whole scope (default), every area of the scope on the sheet showing, or one area (markupId or point). Area beats page beats scope.

angle.description: For set_pattern_direction instead of x1..y2: the direction members run, in degrees on the sheet: 0 across, 90 up it. For get_lines and trace_field: degrees 0..180 with y DOWN, as get_lines reports angles (only lines at that angle / the pattern's stroke direction).

create.description: For trace_area and trace_field: also place the outline as an area of scopeId (or the active scope). Default false: the rings are returned for create_markup.

bridgeGapFeet.description: For trace_area: the widest gap in the linework still treated as closed, in feet. Default 3.5. For trace_field: the widest gap between neighbouring strokes, default measured.

dimension.description: For read_scale: a written dimension, e.g. 12'-6", to check the sheet's scale against; give the two ends it spans as `points`.

replaces.description: For track_addenda with `page`: the ZERO-based page this addendum sheet replaces, to link the two by hand.

markups.description: For create_markups: up to 500 entries, each {kind, rings, scopeId?, page?} as create_markup takes them. One undo step.

inside.description: For get_lines: only lines with both ends inside rect. Default false (lines crossing it are included).

angleTolerance.description: For get_lines orientation, in degrees. Default 1.

dedupe.description: For get_lines: merge a segment drawn twice, in either direction. Default true.

sort.description: For get_lines: longest first (default), left to right, or top to bottom.

maxLengthPoints.description: For get_lines: leave out longer segments, in PDF points.

minLengthFeet.description: For get_lines on a scaled sheet: shortest length kept, in feet.

maxLengthFeet.description: For get_lines on a scaled sheet: longest length kept, in feet.

withoutEmbeddedMarkups.description: For save_copy: leave every other app's markups (Bluebeam's, anyone's) out of the copy. Links stay. Default false.

path.description: For export: an absolute path to write the file to, e.g. C:\\Users\\me\\Desktop\\takeoff.csv. Its folder must exist. Without it, text formats come back in the reply. For import_scopes: the PDF to read scopes from. For close_tab: the tab to close (default: the one showing).

overwrite.description: For export with path: replace a file already there. A PDF is never replaced.

file.description: Optional on every call: the PDF this call is about, as a full path, file name or document id. REDBEAM keeps several PDFs open at once and the call goes to this one, whichever the person is looking at. Leave it out and the call goes to the PDF you opened or named last, so name it whenever you work in more than one. Every result names the file it acted on.

setting.description: For set_setting: an id from get_settings (e.g. takeoff.patternStart); the last part alone (patternStart) works when it names one setting.

dx.description: For update_markup (a move) and duplicate_markups (offset of the copies): normalized [0,1] of the page width, + right.

dy.description: As dx, of the page height, + down.

withMarkups.description: For import_scopes: also bring the other PDF's markups (start this takeoff from that one). Default false: scopes only.

ids.description: Markup ids. For accept_imported, duplicate_markups and select_markups.

all.description: For accept_imported: accept every markup still waiting. For trace_field: also every other field of the same pattern.

degrees.description: For rotate_pages: 90, 180 or 270, clockwise. Takeoff on the sheet turns with it.

withGeometry.description: For list_markups: include each markup's rings. Default false.

includeArchived.description: For list_scopes: also list archived scopes.

sizeFeet.description: For trace_area: roughly how wide the field is, in feet. Give it for anything smaller than a room: the sheet is read finer and small gaps stay open.

snap.description: For trace_area: move the outline onto the drawing's own lines. Default true.

cursor.description: For find_text: the `cursor` a previous call returned, to carry on from there.

offset.description: For get_words, get_lines, list_markups and list_bookmarks: the `nextOffset` a previous call returned.

numberBox.description: The box around the drawing number on the title block: {x0,y0,x1,y1} in NORMALIZED [0,1] page coordinates, y DOWN from the top, NOT PDF points (the space get_words and find_text report boxes in). Only words whose centre is inside are read.

titleBox.description: The box around the drawing title (optional; leave out to read numbers only) on the title block: {x0,y0,x1,y1} in NORMALIZED [0,1] page coordinates, y DOWN from the top, NOT PDF points (the space get_words and find_text report boxes in). Only words whose centre is inside are read.

clear.description: Remove the title block boxes; names set with rename_sheets stay.

page.description: ZERO-based page.

number.description: The drawing number as printed, e.g. A3001.

title.description: The drawing title, e.g. OVERALL SITE PLAN. May be empty.

clear.description: Take this page's name back off.

minWidthFeet.description: For trace_field: parts of the pattern narrower than this, in feet, are not field. Default 1.25.

minCutoutSqFt.description: For trace_field: holes smaller than this are filled. Default 1.5.

minFieldSqFt.description: For trace_field with all: the smallest other field returned.

visual.description: For trace_field: check against the rendered sheet. Default true.

whole.description: For get_lines: return each line as drawn, even the part outside rect. Default false: lines are cut to rect (`cut: true` on the ones that go on past it).

recipe.description: For preview_pattern and save_pattern: the pattern recipe, {version:1, name, units?, layers:[...]}. Layers are tiles (convex shapes in a repeating module), members (runs at set places in a module, for a repeating 'random' layout), lines (runs at a spacing), a built-in product (panels, planks, baffle, baffle_cassette, linear_parts with its specifications), and hardware (counted per piece, module, along a run, per joint, where runs cross another layer, per edge or per area). describe_product {productType:"custom_pattern"} returns the full format and worked examples.

withRecipes.description: For list_patterns: include each recipe in full.

scope.description: For get_bom: only the scopes with this name.

perArea.description: For get_bom: also count every area on its own.

brief.description: For get_bom: each scope's note once, in `notes`.

toPages.description: Several sheets to copy onto: ZERO-based page numbers or sheet numbers as the set prints them ("A4.0").

offsets.description: Per target page, {"<page>":{"dx":..,"dy":..}} normalized, for a sheet that does not line up exactly. Default dx/dy.

perimeter.description: For get_bom: the frame round each scope's field per sheet.

tools.name: redbeam_wait_for_person
tools.description: Call this whenever you STOP for the person: you asked them a question, or reached an approval gate (a scope brief, a scope definition) and will do nothing more until they answer in the chat. `for` says what you need, in a few words: "approve the scope definition". REDBEAM shows "Waiting for you" on your group of tabs, so the person can see the work is paused on them and not stuck. Your tabs stay open exactly as they are. Your next REDBEAM call puts the session back to work; you do not need to undo this.

for.description: What you need from the person, in a few words they would recognise.

tools.name: redbeam_end_session
tools.description: Call this ONCE when the job is done: after the last save, as you give the person your hand back. Also call it if the person tells you to stop, or the job is abandoned. REDBEAM then settles your tabs so the person has nothing to tidy: every PDF you changed is saved and becomes one of the person's own tabs (not shown over what they are looking at), and every PDF you only read is closed. `summary` is one line the person reads beside your finished session: what you produced and where. `keep` names PDFs you only read that the person should still be handed (rarely needed). The answer lists `handedBack` and `closed`, and `why` says for each PDF left open whether you changed it or only read it (a PDF the person is looking at is never closed under them). Do NOT call it at an approval gate or while waiting for an answer: that is redbeam_wait_for_person. After it, this session is over; a new job starts with redbeam_start_session.

summary.description: One line for the person: what was done and where it is. "Takeoff saved in Nokia - BLIND TAKEOFF.pdf: 3 scopes, 1,240 sf."

keep.description: PDFs you only read that should be handed to the person rather than closed, by path or file name.

instructions: REDBEAM is a PDF takeoff app. There are no projects: each PDF holds its own takeoff, and saving writes it into the PDF. THE TAKEOFF SKILL: redbeam_start_session hands you the Maxxit precon-takeoff skill (also the resource redbeam://skill/precon-takeoff). Follow it for any takeoff: scope definition for approval first, then the takeoff. A TAKEOFF, START TO FINISH: 0. redbeam_start_session, once per chat. 1. redbeam_open_file with wait:true. Work on a copy when asked to (redbeam_save_copy, then open the copy). 2. redbeam_list_sheets to find the sheets; redbeam_screenshot to look (with `region` for a sharp close-up); redbeam_find_text for tags and notes. 3. Scale first: redbeam_read_scale reads the scale each sheet states; redbeam_set_page_scale sets it (not undoable, so read what is there first); check it against a written dimension with redbeam_read_scale or redbeam_measure. 4. redbeam_describe_product, then redbeam_create_scope with productType and specifications. The answer's `needs` lists what is still missing. 5. Draw: redbeam_trace_area (a room or a field with a line around it), redbeam_trace_field (a hatched or slatted field whose edge is where the hatch stops) or redbeam_get_lines to find an outline, then redbeam_create_markup (or redbeam_create_markups for many, one undo step). Always pass `page`. Coordinates are normalized 0..1, y down. Read the answer: it carries the id, the measure and any warning. 6. Patterns: redbeam_detect_pattern reads what is drawn (redbeam_detect_grid a drawn panel or tile grid; set_pattern_origin mode grid starts an area on its nearest crossing); redbeam_set_pattern_origin and redbeam_set_pattern_direction set it; redbeam_get_pattern reads it back. 6b. A product REDBEAM does not have (triangle panels, a repeating 'random' baffle module, panels on rails, an open cell with coffers, any hardware): with Settings › Beta › Custom patterns on, redbeam_describe_product {productType:"custom_pattern"} gives the recipe format and examples; redbeam_list_patterns shows what the person already has; redbeam_preview_pattern shows a recipe on the sheet, redbeam_save_pattern keeps it on the scope as a draft for the person to approve. 7. Check: redbeam_list_markups (quantities per markup), redbeam_get_bom (pass `scope` to keep it small, `perArea` for counts per area), redbeam_get_piece_list, and a screenshot. 8. redbeam_save, and read how it went. redbeam_export writes a file when a path is given. Every write lands on your session's own undo (redbeam_undo takes back your last change and never the person's; redbeam_get_history shows who changed what), except scales. Pass `file` when more than one PDF is open, so a write cannot land in the wrong one. redbeam_get_ui_state reports `saved` and `warnings`. WORKING BESIDE A PERSON AND OTHER AGENTS: the person is usually working in REDBEAM too, in tabs of their own, and other agents may be working in theirs. Nothing you do moves the person's view, takes the keyboard, or brings REDBEAM to the front. A PDF you open is YOUR tab, behind theirs. YOUR OWN VIEW: in every PDF, yours or the person's, your session has a view of its own: its own sheet, zoom box, selection and scope. redbeam_go_to_page turns YOUR sheet, redbeam_zoom_to_region frames YOUR view, and redbeam_screenshot shows YOUR sheet; none of them changes what is on the person's screen, and nothing ever asks the person for permission. So work in the person's open PDF exactly as you would in your own: read, look, measure, trace, set scales, draw and delete on any sheet, at any time, while they work on a different sheet or the same one. A call with no `page` acts on your sheet (you start on the sheet the person had showing), so pass `page`, or call redbeam_go_to_page first. redbeam_get_ui_state reports your own sheet and scale, and `person` says where the person is looking. The tool in hand, the panels and the layout preview on screen are the person's: redbeam_set_tool, redbeam_open_panel and redbeam_set_layout_preview change nothing there, and you need none of them, because every result has a tool that returns it. The person sees your work as it lands: your markups appear on the sheet, your cursor shows on the sheet you are on with a line saying what you are doing, and they can click your session in the Agents list to go to your sheet. If they should look at something, say which sheet in your chat; do not try to show it to them. SESSIONS: call redbeam_start_session once at the start of every chat, with a short name for the job, and pass the `session` it returns on every other call. REDBEAM shows the person your app and that name on your group of tabs and beside your cursor. Each chat, and each sub-agent or parallel worker, starts its own session and so gets its own tabs, colour and cursor; never use a session another chat was given. THE LIFE OF A SESSION, and keeping what the person sees true: the person sees your session as Working, Waiting for you, or Finished, and sees beside your cursor what your call in flight is doing. That line comes from your calls, so it is only as true as you keep it. (a) When you stop for the person, at a question or an approval gate, call redbeam_wait_for_person with what you need. Otherwise your group just goes quiet and the person cannot tell paused from stuck. (b) When the job is done, or the person calls it off, call redbeam_end_session with a one-line summary. REDBEAM hands the PDFs you changed to the person as their own tabs and closes the ones you only read. Do not leave a session open after your final message, and do not end it at a gate. (c) Work in few, purposeful calls. Do not poll redbeam_get_ui_state in a loop to look busy, and do not leave a session with nothing to do. (d) One session does one job. A new job in the same chat ends the old session and starts a new one, named for the new job. redbeam_close_tab closes a single tab of yours early; redbeam_end_session settles all of them. The guide at redbeam://guide/working-beside-a-person repeats this section.
